ownership_note: Nevada-headquartered colocation operator; taken private by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors in 2022.
Withdrew from its Nevada data center abatement after approval.
ViaWest was acquired by Peak 10 in 2017; the combined company was renamed Flexential. Flexential is listed as operating in Clark County in the 2026 LCB inventory.
Attributed to EdgeCore in contemporaneous coverage of the March 2018 GOED board meeting. Not confirmed in a GOED primary document; the abatement filings use the MECP1 shell name only.
"Design, LLC" is widely reported as the Alphabet/Google entity used for its Nevada data centers. GOED filings do not name the parent.
Privately held wholesale and colocation operator. Nevada projects filed as "Novva Holdings, LLC" (Clark) and "Novva Reno, LLC" (Storey).
Nevada projects filed as sequentially numbered single-purpose entities (NV11, NV12). Majority-owned by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake.
High-density colocation operator; Reno 1 is its first Nevada facility.

Operates a Washoe County data center with a Reno warehouse subsidiary. Its abatements predate NRS 360.754 (2015) and are therefore not in the data center abatement table; the City of Reno groups them under data centers for comparability.
